assumptions: customer-email tables are customers, newsletter_subscribers and users (users holds sign-in emails of the app's users); support_tickets excluded as above; patients and orgs excluded
record_audit_event can read $auth from an endpoint or function that has it
actions named add/edit/patch/delete; the audit action enum matches the calls
the customer wanted the forever-retry and the loop AI call covered by containment rules rather than by a cap
confusions: The skill's recipe for 'Record who changed what' names a workspace.object_required rule that is only needed when the table is missing; it was unclear whether to include it when the table is being built in the same change. I included it; it warns until push.

Guidance says 'placement: unconditional' for a statement inside a foreach does not count; the support_tickets edit lives in a foreach, so the rule can never pass there. No guidance on the right shape for audits of loop writes.

No check for a task with no retry cap; the skill names 'task retries' as not checked, but 'a background task retrying forever' is exactly what the customer named, so I had to pick the nearest proxy (api.request not inside while).
Recipe's 'Cannot see' list did not mention that a rule cannot tell a customer-email column from other email columns (patients, orgs billing_email).
wished_for: A check or param that caps loop iterations or retry counts on tasks, or flags a while loop with no break/limit.
A recipe for 'AI spend control' that names what a check can and cannot see on cost.
Guidance for unconditional calls when a write is inside a foreach (for example, pass the whole batch to the audit function after the loop).
A way to tag tables by field name in one step with a template (table.tag_required with field_names: email) plus a matching audit recipe.
parse_errors_seen: Parse warnings only for names this change creates: table audit_log and function record_audit_event not on branch (expected)
dry_run_problems_seen: BLOCKED function delete_user_account: Syntax error while parsing 'db.del users {' - Invalid arg: as. Fixed by removing 'as $deleted'. Second dry run clean (exit 0).
why_confidence: AI-in-loop containment is checked directly and matches the $900 case, but a loop call through a function is not seen. The retry case is only partly covered: the while-loop shape is checked, retry counts are not. The audit half covers the three named tables and the four write statements; support_tickets is excluded and batch writes are not checked. Nothing was evaluated (evaluate was not in scope), so every finding is a prediction.
